newsitem.title: UK: Platinum firm on Russian puzzle, gold higher.
newsitem.headline: Platinum firm on Russian puzzle, gold higher.

text.p: Platinum stole the show in nervous precious metals trading on Friday fuelled by continued uncertainty over Russian supplies this year, dealers said.
The Swiss emerged as heavy borrowers of platinum, pushing up the forward rates which is why spot platinum shot up $13.50 to $379.50 an ounce on Thursday and then to $382.50 in New York.
Gold took a back seat after a tense ride this week, trading $1.55 higher at $342.25/$342.75 and within its $340-$345 range.

The reason for the platinum squeeze was unclear but dealers said Thursday's rumour of a gold for platinum/palladium swap between Russia and the Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) was a contributory factor.
Details of such a swap deal have not been confirmed yet.
But one theory is that Russia may have pulled out of the the swap involving 30 tonnes of gold held as collateral against a loan after bureaucratic snares surrounding its PGM exports.
"This is purely something that is happening on its own in platinum. It's either because something has gone astray like this deal, or it's being squeezed," said one platinum dealer.
"The trouble is this situation could change....there are people who can take advantage of the situation and sell."
At 1030 GMT spot platium was quoted at $377.25/$378.25 after touching an intraday high of $380.50. Its sister metal palladium meanwhile was $1.00 easier at $152.50/$153.50.

"Unless there is something like the Russian deal there is no reason why platinum should be short," said the dealer adding that unlike palladium, of which Russia is the world's biggest exporter, platinum shortages can be filled by South Africa.
The platinum market was sent into a backwardation for the first time in a long time and one-month lease rates rocketed to 12-13 percent from about 5.5 earlier in the week, dealers said.
Chartists said the market was looking technically stronger after pushing back above a downtrend that began in May 1995.
Resistance was pegged at $384 to $385, based on an area of congestion and a series of highs in early to mid-March.
A break above that would allow prices to move to $391.00 and $392.50, and within sight of the year's peak at $406.
But players would be wary of any signs that big producer South Africa would jump in to increase supplies, dealers said.
In gold, brokers GNI said while the market was weak it could peak above $345 "to try to shake out the weak shorts."
Silver was static at $4.72/$4.74 after a rollercoaster ride on Thursday touching both ends of its range of $4.85 and $4.65.
